_meta.indication: AIMOVIG is indicated for the preventive treatment of migraine in adults.

pivotal_trials.design: 24-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; patients randomized 1:1:1 to placebo, erenumab 70 mg, or erenumab 140 mg SC monthly after a 4-week baseline period
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change in mean monthly migraine days (MMD) from baseline to the last 3 months of the 24-week double-blind treatment phase
pivotal_trials.n: Placebo n=316, erenumab 70 mg n=312, erenumab 140 mg n=318
pivotal_trials.result: Difference in LSM change in MMD vs placebo: -1.40 for 70 mg and -1.85 for 140 mg; 50% MMD responder rates 26.6% placebo, 43.3% (70 mg), 50.0% (140 mg)

nct_ctgov.title: Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Erenumab (AMG 334) in Migraine Prevention

pivotal_trials.design: 12-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; patients randomized 1:1 to placebo or erenumab 70 mg SC monthly after a 4-week baseline period
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change in MMD from baseline to the last month of the 12-week double-blind treatment phase
pivotal_trials.result: Difference in LSM change in MMD (70 mg vs placebo) = -1.04 (95% CI -1.61, -0.47), p < 0.001; 50% MMD responders 29.5% placebo vs 39.7% (70 mg), p = 0.010

nct_ctgov.title: Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Erenumab (AMG 334) Compared to Placebo in Migraine Prevention

pivotal_trials.design: 12-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; adults 18-65 with ≥15 headache days/month and ≥8 migraine days/month, randomized 3:2:2 to placebo, erenumab 70 mg, or erenumab 140 mg
pivotal_trials.population: Adults 18-65 with chronic migraine (≥15 headache days/month, ≥8 migraine days/month)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change in MMD from baseline to the last 4 weeks of the 12-week double-blind treatment phase
pivotal_trials.n: 667 randomized: placebo 286, erenumab 70 mg 191, erenumab 140 mg 190
pivotal_trials.result: Difference in LSM change in MMD vs placebo: -2.46 (95% CI -3.52, -1.39) for 70 mg and -2.45 (95% CI -3.52, -1.38) for 140 mg, p < 0.001 for both; 50% MMD responders 23.5% placebo, 39.9% (70 mg), 41.2% (140 mg)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥3% and more often than placebo) were injection site reactions and constipation. In Studies 1-3, injection site reactions occurred in 6% (70 mg) and 5% (140 mg) vs 3% placebo; constipation in 1% (70 mg) and 3% (140 mg) vs 1% placebo. No serious safety issues had a clear causal relationship to erenumab.
target_moa: Erenumab-aooe is a human IgG2 monoclonal antibody that binds to the calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) receptor and antagonizes CGRP receptor function; it is the first product of this class.

advisory_committee.vote: The application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee.

summary.text: Aimovig (erenumab-aooe) was submitted as a BLA received 5/17/2017 under a Standard review and approved 5/17/2018 for the preventive treatment of migraine in adults as a first-in-class CGRP receptor antagonist. No accelerated approval, breakthrough, orphan, or priority designations were used; efficacy rested on three adequate and well-controlled trials and the application was not referred to an advisory committee.

citations.quote: Please refer to your Biologics License Application (BLA) dated and received May 17, 2017, and your amendments, submitted under section 351(a) of the Public Health Service Act for Aimovig (erenumab-aooe) injection 70 mg/mL.
Erenumab is a human monoclonal antibody that antagonizes the calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) receptor. It is the first product of this class to be reviewed in an FDA marketing application.

This application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because it was clear that the applicant had provided substantial evidence of effectiveness from three adequate and well controlled studies, using clinical trial designs similar to those of trials for previously approved migraine drugs.

requirement.text: PMR 3392-2: An open-label pharmacokinetic, safety, and tolerability study in pediatric migraine patients ages 6 through 11 years, to identify doses matching adult 70-mg and 140-mg exposures.

citations.quote: PMR 3392-2 An open-label pharmacokinetic, safety, and tolerability study in pediatric migraine patients ages 6 through 11 years. Dosing will depend on body weight, according to two weight bands: <40 kg and ≥40 kg. The study should identify doses that provide exposures that match those observed with the 70-mg and 140-mg doses of Aimovig in adults.
